summary.headline: IFB Industries Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14.04% to INR1,512 crore, but PBDIT margin fell to 6.01% from 7.73% on commodity and forex pressure.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 14.04% YoY to INR1,512 crore, while PBDIT fell 11.3% to INR90.92 crore and margin compressed about 172 bps to 6.01%. PAT declined to INR39.56 crore from INR49.75 crore, with management attributing the squeeze to material cost inflation from commodities and a weaker rupee. Management said price hikes have not recovered the cost increase and that the 10% appliance EBITDA margin target is no longer intact. Engineering was described as on budget, with new EV-focused capex in Gujarat and a planned chain plant, and the Sanand Tata project proceeding.

financial_highlights.metric: Share of loss from associate (IFB Refrigeration, H1)

segments.name: Home Appliances
segments.commentary: Management said Q1 grew 18% and Q2 grew 10.5%, with H1 growth at about 14.5% versus 9.8% for full FY26. Washer share was held or slightly up, and microwave and dishwasher share rose; AC and refrigerator shares remain small.

segments.name: Engineering
segments.commentary: Budget was met on top line and bottom line, with growth from fine blanking and stampings. Mix is about 50% two-wheeler, 40% four-wheeler, and 10% electrical and three-wheeler; order booking is INR220 crore against a INR500 crore target.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Furnace annealing capacity was raised from 1,500-1,700 tons to 2,800 tons per month, and management is stabilising the ramp. Sales split is about 60% internal and 40% external.

segments.name: Commercial washing machines
segments.commentary: Management claims about 20-25% market share and number one position; market estimated at INR400-500 crore against INR104 crore of revenue last year.

segments.name: Associate: IFB Refrigeration
segments.commentary: Associate loss widened to INR6.23 crore in H1 from INR3.23 crore, driven by oil-linked material costs rising 8-10%.

guidance_outlook: Home appliances: management reiterated the aim of about 20% growth as aspirational, with H1 at about 14.5%; Q3 expected to be strong given Diwali shift to 8 November 2026 from 20 October 2025.
Appliance 10% EBITDA margin target: management said it is not intact; without the roughly 4.3% BOM increase, margin would have been close to 10%.
Engineering: management said it does not give formal guidance but expects the same growth pattern if markets do not slump; H2 should be around the current level.
Gujarat EV four-wheeler facility (INR102-103 crore capex, 100% EV products) expected to start manufacturing around September-October 2027; capex in two phases, FY27 and FY28.
Capex: H1 FY27 capex of INR28.58 crore (Q1 INR12.43 crore, Q2 INR16.15 crore); CWIP of INR39.5 crore expected to capitalise over about 7-8 months.
Advance tax paid: about INR11 crore in Q1 and INR14 crore in Q2.
Battery Can project in Gujarat to follow a 1:1 debt-to-equity funding policy; a broader funding policy for the engineering expansion has not been finalised.
capex_capacity: Gujarat EV four-wheeler plant: land acquired, under construction, capex about INR103 crore, manufacturing expected Sept-Oct 2027.
Own chain plant being set up because chain imports were restricted by government guidelines.
Steel furnace annealing capacity raised to 2,800 tons per month from 1,500-1,700 tons.
Engineering technology centre set up in Switzerland to transfer cost-reduction technology to plants.
Tata project in Sanand: LOI received and factory construction started.
Appliances: 11 kg front loader is the top product; no 12 kg offering yet, which is identified as a product gap.
demand_pricing: Front loaders: management said share is maintained despite intense competition; market is shifting toward 8 kg and above, and 12 kg and above is a significant segment where IFB has only an 11 kg product.
Price hikes: management said industry price hikes have not covered BOM inflation; large-appliance pricing is being held back for competitiveness during festive season.
Scheme discipline: trade schemes are now tied to partner volume commitments, with graded payouts for under-delivery; management denied a scheme-cut programme.
Distribution: focus on weighted distribution at key outlets, not numerical distribution; south is the largest region, followed by west, north and east.
Engineering order book: INR220 crore booked against INR500 crore target, including ICE, EV-lucrative and EV-profitable businesses.
Staff costs fell in Q2 as about 100 positions were left unfilled; sales promotion including CSR fell to INR75 crore from INR81 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10% EBITDA margin target for appliances still intact given commodity and forex pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Abraham said no. Material costs rose about 4 percentage points of net revenue and BOM rose about 4.3%; price hikes have fallen short of this.

qa_highlights.question: Why has growth slowed to 10.5% in Q2 and is 20% still the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the Q2 slowdown to Diwali shifting into Q3 (8 November 2026 versus 20 October 2025). H1 grew about 14.5%, and 20% was called aspirational.

qa_highlights.question: Why did rent (lease) cash outflows rise sharply, and why did H1 operating profit appear to fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Soumitra Goswami said the increase relates to ROU assets, mainly the Gujarat plant lease. Principal repayments rose from INR19 crore to INR57 crore, and the lease cost sits below PBDIT. He deferred part of the detailed reconciliation offline.

qa_highlights.question: Should engineering be demerged, and are there plans to consolidate plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Arup Das said there is no demerger proposal at present. Soumitra Goswami said there is no current plan to consolidate the 10 manufacturing facilities.

qa_highlights.question: What are the engineering capex, asset turnover and H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of about INR103 crore is planned for the Gujarat EV plant in two phases (FY27 and FY28). Asset turnover was not answered and management would revert.

qa_highlights.question: Is the industry taking price increases, and why are margins under pressure versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Abraham said large-appliance pricing could be higher but is held back by competitiveness and a cautious industry stance in the festive period. Small appliances have a lower ticket-size sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Is IFB open to using debt for expansion and any acquisition updates?
qa_highlights.answer: Soumitra Goswami said the policy has been 1:1 debt to equity, with the engineering expansion under review and no decision yet. Arup Das said more than 72 companies have been evaluated for synergy and non-disruptive products.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from commodity and forex inflation with incomplete price pass-through; BOM up about 4.3%.
Q3 Diwali-driven growth needs to offset a muted Q2; management has not given formal guidance.
Trade scheme payouts tied to volumes could affect channel reaction and shelf presence.
Associate IFB Refrigeration loss widened to INR6.23 crore in H1 from INR3.23 crore.
Competition in front loaders and the 12 kg+ capacity segment, where IFB lacks a product.
Rising lease principal payments (INR57 crore in H1 versus INR19 crore) and a potential shift away from net cash policy.
Management did not give asset turnover figures and deferred the rent reconciliation offline; an open disclosure question.
summary.management_tone: Confident on engineering and the growth outlook but cautious on margins; management conceded the 10% appliance margin target is off track. Several answers were deferred or unanswered (asset turnover, rent reconciliation), and audio quality was poor for parts of the call.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Home appliances grew about 14.5% in H1 (Q1 18%, Q2 10.5%), with Q3 expected strong as Diwali moves to 8 Nov 2026 from 20 Oct 2025; the ~20% target is called aspirational, and engineering expects the same growth pattern with order book INR220 crore against a INR500 crore target.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Engineering expansion is under review with its funding policy not finalised, and the Battery Can project will follow a 1:1 debt-to-equity policy; H1 FY27 capex was only INR28.58 crore, so no large new program is yet committed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no formal guidance, called the ~20% home appliance growth aspirational against H1 at about 14.5%, and conceded the 10% margin target is off track.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: PBDIT fell 11.3% in Q2 to INR90.92 crore with margin at 6.01% versus 7.73%, PAT fell to INR39.56 crore from INR49.75 crore, and the associate loss widened to INR6.23 crore in H1 from INR3.23 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management flagged a 12 kg+ front loader gap (IFB has only an 11 kg model in a segment it calls significant), but no launch date was given.

rows.label: Price pass-through of BOM inflation
rows.why: BOM rose about 4.3% and price hikes have not covered it, but large-appliance pricing is being held back for competitiveness during the festive season, so a catch-up depends on competitors moving.

rows.label: Engineering order book vs target
rows.why: INR220 crore booked against a INR500 crore target, with management expecting H2 at about the current run rate if markets do not slump.

rows.label: Lease cash outflow step-up
rows.why: Principal lease repayments rose to INR57 crore in H1 from INR19 crore, mainly from the Gujarat plant ROU asset, and this moves the policy away from a net cash position.
